criteria.description: Adults aged 18 years or older undergoing cardiac surgery.
Animal studies, participants younger than 18 years, or studies exclusively outside cardiac surgery.
Intravenous dexmedetomidine administered before, during, or after cardiac surgery.
No dexmedetomidine intervention or dexmedetomidine given only by a non-intravenous route.
No placebo or normal saline control; an active drug comparator alone is inappropriate.
Not a randomized controlled trial, such as an observational study, review, or meta-analysis.
Published from 1 January 2014 through 10 March 2024, inclusive.
Published before 1 January 2014 or after 10 March 2024.

Postoperative delirium (primary), intensive care unit length of stay, mortality, bradycardia, or hypotension (secondary). Delirium assessments use CAM-ICU in ICU and CAM on the ward; 12-hour assessments are eligible.

Confirmed insufficient or non-extractable data for the protocol outcomes. Missing information in a title or abstract alone does not confirm non-extractability; retain for full-text assessment and possible author contact.

research_question: In adults undergoing cardiac surgery, does intravenous dexmedetomidine, compared with placebo or normal saline, reduce postoperative delirium, affect intensive-care-unit length of stay or mortality, or alter the risks of bradycardia and hypotension?
title: Dexmedetomidine for delirium prevention in adult patients following cardiac surgery
